newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-COPPIN STATE UPSETS SOUTH CAROLINA.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-COPPIN STATE UPSETS SOUTH CAROLINA.

text.p: So where is Coppin State? In the second round of the NCAA men's basketball tournament, that's where.

Danny Singletary came off the bench to score 22 points and Antoine Brockington added 20 as the boys from Baltimore became just the third 15th-seeded team ever to win a first-round game by stunning second seed South Carolina 77-63 in the East Region in Pittsburgh.
The Eagles also provided the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference its first-ever win in the tournament, snapping a 16-game losing streak shared by five schools since 1981.
"This one today has to go down as one of the major, major wins in my life," said Coppin State coach Ron "Fang" Mitchell.

"We go in a tremendous underdog, and the MEAC had never won a game in the history of the NCAA, and for us to come in here and carry the MEAC banner and do the job that these young people did today, it just felt great."

B.J. McKie scored 16 points and Melvin Watson 13 for South Carolina (25-7), which had its storybook season cut short. The Gamecocks captured the Southeastern Conference regular-season title and beat defending champion Kentucky twice in the regular season.
"Congratulations to Coppin State," said South Carolina coach Eddie Fogler. "Without a doubt, they were easily the better team here today. Their zones bothered us offensively."
"We utilized our matchup zone and started throwing different defences at them to try to slow them down and work for a shot," said Mitchell
The only 15th seeds previously to upset a second seed in the first round since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985 were Richmond (over Syracuse in 1991) and Santa Clara (over Arizona in 1993).
Coppin State will play 10th-seeded Texas, a 71-58 winner over Wisconsin, in the second round on Sunday.
The Gamecocks were the second high-seeded SEC team to be upset Friday. Georgia, seeded third in the Southeast Region, lost to 14th-seeded Chattanooga in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Willie Young hit two running shots in the lane in the final 91 seconds to secure the win.
Young finished with 24 points for the Moccasins (23-10), who will next play Illinois, a 90-77 winner over the University of Southern California.
Also in the Southeast, Austin Croshere scored a season-high 39 points as 10th-seeded Providence missed just six shots in the first half en route to an 81-59 demolition of seventh-seeded Marquette.

Derrick Brown added 13 points for the Friars, who advanced to the second round for the first time since 1987, when it reached the Final Four under coach Rick Pitino, now with defending champion Kentucky.

Providence will next face Duke. Jeff Capel scored 25 points and Trajan Langdon hit a big basket as the second-seeded Blue Devils survived a late scare before posting a 71-68 victory over 15th-seeded Murray State.
Duke is back in the second round for the first time since 1994, when it advanced to the championship game before losing to Arkansas.
In the West Region at Tucson, Arizona, Tim Duncan won the battle in the pivot with 22 points and 22 rebounds as third-seeded Wake Forest routed 14th-seeded St. Mary's of California 64-46.
Brad Millard, the huge centre known as "Big Continent," scored 16 points for St. Mary's, which was in the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 1989.
Wake will face sixth-seeded Stanford next. Kris Weems scored 20 points and Brevin Knight 18 as Stanford used a second-half run to break open a tight game and defeat 11th-seeded Oklahoma 80-67.
Nate Erdmann, the only Sooner to hit a field goal in the final eight minutes, led Oklahoma with 23 points.
Keith Van Horn scored 12 of his 16 points in the first half as second-seeded Utah coasted to a 75-61 victory over 15th-seeded Navy.
Michael Doleac scored 19 points for the Utes, who will play seventh-seeded NC-Charlotte Sunday. NC-Charlotte beat 10th seed Georgetown 79-67.

In the Midwest Region in Kansas City, top seed Minnesota disposed of 16th seed Southwest Texas 78-46 and will face ninth-seeded Temple, which cruised to a 62-40 victory over eighth-seeded Mississippi.
Clemson coach Rick Barnes picked up his first NCAA Tournament victory in five tries as his fourth-seeded team rolled to a 68-56 victory over 13th-seeded Miami of Ohio.
The Tigers will play fifth-seeded Tulsa, which routed 12th seed Boston University 81-52.
Back in the East, Kenny Thomas redeemed himself with a key rebound and two free throws in the final three seconds as third-seeded New Mexico edged 14th-seeded Old Dominion 59-55.

Thomas, who missed a pair of free throws with 19.8 seconds to play, grabbed the rebound of an E.J. Sherod miss and was fouled with 2.4 seconds left. He went to the line and sank both free throws for a 59-55 lead.
New Mexico next will face sixth seed Louiville, a 65-57 victor over Massachusetts.
